rows: Five Suns
Aztec: 4 previous world-ages destroyed; current is the 5th; requires sacrifice to continue
Why sacrifice?
The gods gave their lives to create the sun; humans owe cosmic debt; sacrifice repays it
Quetzalcóatl
Feathered serpent; wind/sky/Venus; trickster rival to Tezcatlipoca; promised return
Huitzilopochtli
Aztec tribal/sun/war god; born fully armed; defeats moon (Coyolxauhqui) and stars at dawn
Tlaloc
Rain god; requires children's tears; Tlalocan = paradise for water-death victims
Aztec underworld
Mictlan — 9 levels; four-year journey; moral neutrality; burial goods matter
Popol Vuh
K'iche' Maya creation epic; Hero Twins defeat Xibalba; maize humans are the 4th creation
Hero Twins
Hunahpu and Xbalanque; defeat lords of Xibalba; become sun and moon
Xibalba
Maya underworld; 12 lords; 6 houses of ordeal; actively hostile, not passive
Ball game significance
Ritual enactment of solar cycle; liminal space; can involve sacrifice
Maya creation material
Maize (4th attempt); human vision intentionally limited by the gods
Inca creator
Viracocha — created at Lake Titicaca; walked west across the ocean
Inca solar deity
Inti (sun); Emperor = Inti's son; Coricancha = Temple of the Sun
Ceque system
41 lines from Coricancha; 328 sacred sites (huacas) = the city as cosmological map
Pachamama
Andean earth mother; still actively worshipped; older than Inca state religion
Aztec 52-year cycle
Two calendars align; New Fire Ceremony at end — world might end if Pleiades don't pass
